title: Add runnable streaming + tool-calling samples (multi-tool loop + tool_result messages)
author: Renee Sullivan
release_notes:
- Add runnable streaming + tool-calling samples (Python/TS/Go) with consistent event handling and a tool-result loop.
- Document common pitfalls (partial tool args mid-stream, stream disconnects) and recommended handling.
description:
Context: As part of the cross-SDK/docs examples refresh, we need copy/paste runnable samples that demonstrate the canonical streaming mental model *and* the supported tool-calling semantics (including partial tool-call arguments during streaming and the tool_result message loop). Support and SE feedback shows users frequently get stuck on (a) assembling deltas into a final assistant message, (b) handling tool-call args that arrive in multiple chunks, and (c) what to send back after executing a tool.

What this PR adds: 1) New runnable samples in this repo for Python, TypeScript, and Go that: - Stream a chat completion - Detect tool_call deltas during the stream - Assemble tool-call arguments incrementally (string buffer -> JSON parse) - Execute one or more tools (including parallel tool calls when multiple tool calls are emitted) - Send tool_result messages back to the model - Continue the loop until the assistant returns a final message. 2) A unified README pattern across samples: consistent env vars, install/run steps, and expected console output. 3) A small local "fixture transcript" (golden-ish) used by a smoke test to prevent examples from silently drifting (we are not trying to lock model output; we are locking the event-handling flow and message shapes).

Design notes (aligns with DevEx conventions): - Streaming consumption uses event-type branching and does *not* assume that tool-call arguments arrive in a single event. - We treat tool-call args as a byte/str stream: append deltas, attempt JSON parse when "final" is observed, and surface a clear error with a suggested retry strategy when parse fails. - Tool results are sent as tool_result messages keyed by tool_call_id. - The samples show minimal logging that helps debug: event type, tool name, tool_call_id, and a truncated args preview. - We intentionally avoid model-specific features beyond the documented tool-calling contract; README includes a short note to choose a model that supports tool calling.

Sample shape (illustrative, see language dirs for the real code): while streaming: - on message.delta: append assistant content delta - on tool_call.delta: append args delta to a per-call buffer - on tool_call.final: JSON.parse args buffer, enqueue tool execution - on message.error: print and exit with non-zero status. After stream completes: for each tool call -> run tool -> append tool_result -> send another request (non-streaming by default for simplicity, streaming optional flag).

Why in redwood-examples vs SDK repos: These are meant to be runnable end-to-end with minimal context and referenced directly from docs (streaming guide + tool calling guide). SDK repos will still contain smaller snippet-level examples, but the runnable version belongs here.

Test plan: - `make test` runs lint + a smoke test that imports/compiles each sample and validates it can execute the non-network parts (schema / arg parsing) deterministically. - Manual: run each sample against Hosted API with `REDWOOD_API_KEY` set; confirm tool loop completes and final assistant message prints.

Risk/mitigations: - Model variability: README calls out model support and provides a fallback section (try a different model if tool calls are not emitted). - Partial args: we explicitly buffer + parse and link to SUP-18421 guidance. - Streaming disconnects: examples include a simple retry note (idempotency guidance lives in docs; we keep sample small).

Follow-ups: - Pair with docs PR to link directly to these samples and keep parity with SDK snippet conventions (tracked in ENG-4826). - After merge, add these sample directories to the snippet-sync CI check in the monorepo (separate PR).

conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Please ensure the event naming in logs matches the Confluence conventions (delta vs final), and that tool_call_id is always printed (it’s essential for debugging multi-call streams). Also, can we show the buffering behavior explicitly so users don’t assume args are complete on first delta?

Renee Sullivan (author): Updated all three samples to use `tool_call.delta` / `tool_call.final` terminology in log lines and added `tool_call_id` to each tool-related log. Also added a short comment above the args buffer map explaining why we buffer and when we attempt JSON parse.

Brian Murphy (review): In TS sample, we should avoid implying tool args are trustworthy. Can we add a small runtime validation step (even if minimal) and a clear error message that points to retry guidance?

Renee Sullivan (author): Added a lightweight guard in TS: validate parsed args is an object and that required keys exist per tool (e.g., `city` for weather). On failure we print a structured error and exit 2. README now has a “If JSON parse fails / args incomplete” troubleshooting note.
Wei Chen (review): README top-level should clarify required env vars and exact run commands; also avoid referencing unreleased SDK APIs. These are examples repo, but users will copy/paste blindly.

Renee Sullivan (author): Standardized env vars: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, optional `REDWOOD_BASE_URL`, and `REDWOOD_MODEL`. Removed any mention of unreleased SDK helpers; all samples call the public REST endpoints or released SDK entrypoints depending on language, with pinned versions in package/go.mod requirements.
Sabrina James (review): Smoke test is good; can we make it non-flaky by not calling the network in CI? Also please keep expected output blocks small.

Renee Sullivan (author): CI smoke test is offline only (build/typecheck + unit-like checks for arg parsing and tool dispatch). Network run remains manual. Trimmed expected output blocks to show only key lines (event types + final message).
Ibrahim Khan (approval): Looks aligned with parity conventions and addresses partial tool args pitfall. Approved.
Wei Chen (approval): Approved with minor wording tweaks already applied.
